scope: audit-only; does not authorize object identity, attributes, delivery edges, or Unit uses

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Deployment Skill that lets the user place carried Weapons or Equipment
factsEvidence: When the user deploys, they may place the allowed number of carried Weapons or Equipment
reviews.caveat: Minelayer is a deployment method for the user's source-listed items, not a separate deployed-object identity. It cannot authorize a generic Mine variant or reverse Unit ownership.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Common Skill used to place eligible
factsEvidence: The user places one eligible Token or Model without a Roll
reviews.caveat: Place Deployable defines a placement method for eligible source-listed items; its generic Token/Model wording is not a new object identity or a blanket delivery edge.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Call two Speedball Tokens
factsEvidence: During the Active Turn, place two 55 mm Speedball Tokens
Request Speedball cannot be performed partway through the Order Expenditure Sequence.
reviews.caveat: N5.3 p. 84 explicitly defines Speedball Tokens as State Tokens for support drops, not as standard targetable Deployable Weapon/Equipment profiles. The Tokens and their single-use contents have no reviewed ARM/BTS/STR/S source profile here and must not receive inferred reverse uses.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Token represents a [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapon or piece of Equipment on the battlefield.
reviews.caveat: Glossary term for an on-table representation, not a separate object profile. Resolve any particular Token to its actual source Weapon or Equipment and reviewed delivery before publishing uses.

reviews.summaryEvidence: This token is a reminder placed to indicate the effect of a rule, Skill, or game state
reviews.caveat: A State Token indicates an effect and is not automatically a targetable Deployable. Specific Speedball and SpecBall tokens are classified by their own source clauses.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Equipment with the [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Trait can be placed as an independent battlefield game element
reviews.caveat: Generic Deployable Equipment terminology provides neither a concrete Equipment identity nor four-attribute values; review each source item separately.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Weapon with the [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Trait can be placed as an independent battlefield game element
reviews.caveat: Generic Deployable Weapon terminology is not an object instance or source-specific delivery edge; source Weapon and mode must be verified separately.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Scenery Element is a battlefield game element representing scenery or terrain
reviews.caveat: Scenery Element is a class of battlefield game elements, not one universal scenery profile. Deployable Cover remains a separately reviewed S3 example; other scenery requires its own source evidence.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Place the 55 mm Token via [[skill:combat-jump|Combat Jump]] with PH 15
factsEvidence: Outside the [[rule:order-expenditure-sequence|Order Expenditure Sequence]], place one 55 mm SpecBall Token
SpecBall Tokens are [[term:state-token|State Tokens]]: they do not block enemy Movement and cannot be selected as targets for [[equipment:deactivator|Deactivators]].
reviews.caveat: N5.3 p. 98 describes one SpecBall State Token collected by an eligible Spec-Ops Trooper; it is distinct from the two Speedballs in Request Speedball (p. 84). Neither drop Token is a standard targetable four-attribute Deployable. A SpecBot selected as a SpecBall item requires separate evidence and is not classified here.

reviews.summaryEvidence: assigns the user's profile-listed MODs to one deployed Remote
factsEvidence: When the user is deployed, the player places a RemDriver Token beside one Remote already deployed on the game table.
The RemDriver Token is removed at the end of the Order in which the user enters any Null State.
reviews.caveat: RemDriver Token marks a Remote receiving MODs from a separate Trooper. It is not an independently deployed Weapon/Equipment profile, delivery edge or additional Remote carrier.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Peripheral type with unlimited operating distance that starts undeployed
factsEvidence: An Ancillary [[skill:peripheral|Peripheral]] does not deploy with its Controller. The Controller may place it later using [[skill:place-deployable|Place Deployable]]
reviews.caveat: N5.3 pp. 107-108 explicitly allow a Controller to place its Ancillary Peripheral, which then uses Peripheral activation rules. This is a Peripheral Trooper with its own source Unit/Profile relationships, not a Weapon/Equipment four-stat object or generic source-weapon reverse use. Whether a dedicated peripheral-object reference is needed remains open.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Rules for Carrying Supply Boxes.
factsEvidence: Keep the Supply Box Token on the table even if its carrier becomes classified as Null.
reviews.caveat: Supply Box Tokens belong to the core Supplies scenario, with scenario-specific representation, carrying and control rules. They are concrete objective elements, not source Weapon/Equipment Deployables or Army roster items; an objective catalog would need separate provenance and presentation.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Short Skill used by Specialist Troops to collect a Supply Box.
factsEvidence: The Specialist must be in Silhouette contact with a Supply Box Token not being carried by a Model
reviews.caveat: Pick Up Supply Boxes is a scenario Skill acting on a Supplies objective. It creates no additional Supply Box identity, general Deployable placement edge, or Weapon/Equipment Unit use.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapon or Equipment is placed as an independent battlefield element
reviews.caveat: Deployable describes an eligible Weapon/Equipment class and its general consequences; it does not establish a concrete deployed object, carrier, mode or four-stat profile. Existing reviewed objects remain individually identified.

reviews.summaryEvidence: When placed, applies [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] and Perimeter
factsEvidence: When using [[skill:place-deployable|Place Deployable]], a destination wholly inside the user's [[trait:zone-of-control-zc|Zone of Control]] replaces the usual Silhouette contact.
The placed item becomes active at the Conclusion of the Order and remains stationary.
reviews.caveat: Perimeter changes placement and subsequent behavior for an eligible item. It is not a canonical object identity and cannot equate Crazykoala, Madtraps, WildParrot, FastPanda or other items.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Once in play, a Boost weapon must trigger
reviews.caveat: Boost describes how an already placed eligible Weapon triggers, moves, detonates and is removed. It does not establish another object or authorize equivalence with Mines; placement, CAMO exceptions and source-specific effects remain separate.

reviews.summaryEvidence: or placing a [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapon under its specific conditions
factsEvidence: To place a [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapon whose Trigger Area contains an enemy [[state:camouflaged|Camouflaged]] Marker
reviews.caveat: Intuitive Attack is a conditional declaration and WIP-based delivery method, not a Weapon subtype or a new deployed object. Whether it applies must be reviewed for each item and its placement requirements.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Common Skill for evading applicable Attacks and repositioning
factsEvidence: Dodge movement occurs in the Effects step, follows the General Movement Rules, and does not generate reactions or trigger [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapons or Equipment.
reviews.caveat: Dodge defines an evasion and movement exception to Deployable triggering; a Dodge-related Token or MOD mention does not introduce a separate battlefield object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: An Automatic Special Skill that limits ARO generation
factsEvidence: Stealth does not prevent [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapons or Equipment from triggering.
reviews.caveat: Stealth affects reaction eligibility, not the identity, activation or delivery edge of a Deployable. Its triggering exception must not be interpreted as an additional source carrier.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Long Common Skill that can move a Trooper without generating enemy AROs
factsEvidence: With [[skill:stealth|Stealth]] in the Active Turn, the user may declare [[skill:cautious-movement|Cautious Movement]]
reviews.caveat: Cautious Movement's ARO and Stealth interactions do not suppress eligible Deployable triggering or define a deployed object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: After surviving one or more successful Attacks
factsEvidence: Movement after failing a Guts Roll follows general movement and measuring requirements. It does not generate [[trait:aro|AROs]], trigger [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapons or Equipment
reviews.caveat: Guts Roll movement is a rule-specific exemption from triggering Deployables, not another battlefield object, delivery route or carrier context.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Peripheral type with unlimited operating distance and a maximum of three per Controller
factsEvidence: Up to three Control [[skill:peripheral|Peripherals]] form a Control Unit. Designate one [[skill:peripheral|Peripheral]] as Spearhead with a Spearhead Token
reviews.caveat: The Spearhead Token indicates a Control Unit role held by a Peripheral Trooper, not an additional independent Weapon/Equipment Deployable or troop profile.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Peripheral type granted by [[skill:cyberplug]]
factsEvidence: If two deploy, one must be Connected and the other Autonomous. Mark Autonomous units with an Autonomous Token.
reviews.caveat: The Autonomous Token marks which Cyberplug Peripheral Trooper operates in the Autonomous Profile. It is not a separate deployed object or an excuse to derive Controller/Army ownership from the Token.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Marker State that hides the represented Trooper, Weapon, or Equipment
factsEvidence: A successful [[skill:discover]] Roll reveals the Marker and replaces it with the corresponding Model or Token.
reviews.caveat: A Camouflaged Marker is a representation of an existing Trooper, Weapon or Equipment. The Marker does not define a generic Mine or a new independent object identity; its represented item must be resolved separately.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A disguise State that represents the bearer as another same-faction Trooper
factsEvidence: A Trooper in [[state:holomask|HoloMask State]] cannot copy [[skill:hacker]] or Hackable status or items with the [[trait:deployable]] Trait represented by Tokens or Models.
reviews.caveat: HoloMask changes a Trooper's presentation and explicitly excludes copying Deployable items represented by Tokens or Models. Neither the disguise nor its restriction creates a new deployed-object profile.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Long Special Skill that keeps the user off-table
factsEvidence: A failed landing moves the user to the player's Deployment Zone edge
reviews.caveat: Combat Jump affects the Trooper and independently sourced carried deployables. A failed landing removes placed eligible items; no generic object identity or carrier link is created.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Deployment Skill that lets the user deploy forward while disguised
factsEvidence: A failed WIP Roll places the user in their own Deployment Zone
reviews.caveat: Impersonation's failed deployment removes eligible carried Deployables and changes the Trooper's representation; no new object profile follows.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Deployment Skill that allows forward deployment
factsEvidence: If the Roll fails, the user is moved to their own Deployment Zone edge
reviews.caveat: Failed Infiltration removes independently sourced deployed equipment/weapons accompanying the Trooper; it does not define a device variant or ownership edge.

reviews.summaryEvidence: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that grants one activation
factsEvidence: During the Tactical Phase, place an Impetuous Token next to the user
reviews.caveat: Impetuous Tokens mark a Trooper's activation entitlement and are removed when spent; they are not independent deployed Weapon or Equipment profiles.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A State applied when an army enters Retreat!
factsEvidence: [[state:retreat|Retreat!]] ends when the army leaves the Retreat! situation
reviews.caveat: Retreat! and Command Token references govern an existing Trooper/Army State, not a separate deployed game element; Marker cancellation changes representation only.

reviews.summaryEvidence: An optional Automatic Special Skill that lets an [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] Trooper
factsEvidence: The user can be healed; removing one Wound returns it to [[state:normal]] and removes the NWI Token.
reviews.caveat: NWI Token indicates an existing Trooper's condition and is removed on recovery. It is not a targetable deployed object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Protheion uses Wounds inflicted through a [[skill:cc-attack]]
factsEvidence: Indicate the increase with a Power-Up 1 or Power-Up 2 Token.
reviews.caveat: Power-Up Tokens track an existing Trooper's increased VITA; they do not define new Weapon/Equipment or Trooper identities.

reviews.summaryEvidence: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill that represents one Trooper through two or three Proxy Models
factsEvidence: Marker and [[state:hidden-deployment|Hidden Deployment]] status are not canceled merely by placing or assigning the Active Proxy Token.
reviews.caveat: The Active Proxy Token identifies the active Proxy of an existing G: Jumper Trooper. It is a status/role indicator, not an independent object or Unit.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Rules for Dominate Quadrants.
factsEvidence: Tokens and Markers for weapons, Equipment, or anything other than a Trooper do not contribute Victory Points.
reviews.caveat: Domination excludes Weapon/Equipment Tokens and Markers from the scoring rule. This is an objective eligibility restriction, not a new deployed object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Short Special Skill that normally recovers a [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] VITA Trooper
factsEvidence: Doctor (2W) removes two Wounds on successful ordinary recovery.
reviews.caveat: Doctor is recovery and State cancellation; its Command Token rerolls concern a spendable resource, not a deployed Token or newly created target identity.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Short Special Skill that repairs STR targets
factsEvidence: With [[skill:remote-presence|Remote Presence]], one successful repair Roll removes enough Wounds
reviews.caveat: Engineer repairs existing STR targets or cancels States. Command Token rerolls do not create an object or establish a carrier.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Level 2 of [[skill:strategos]].
factsEvidence: During the Tactical Phase's Executive Use of Command Tokens step
reviews.caveat: Strategos L2 moves Troopers and Peripherals between Combat Groups without Command Token expenditure. This is a command effect, not a Token or deployed object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: An obligatory Automatic Special Skill for STR Troopers
factsEvidence: When [[skill:engineer]] or another rule explicitly permits it, Command Tokens may reroll the failed repair Roll.
reviews.caveat: Remote Presence changes a STR Trooper's Unconscious behavior; the Command Token reroll refers to a resource rather than a standalone battlefield object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A [[skill:hacker]] can use Hacking Programs within their Hacking Area
factsEvidence: The Hacking Area includes the [[skill:hacker]]'s own [[trait:zone-of-control-zc|Zone of Control]]
reviews.caveat: Hacking Area uses existing Repeater and Deployable Repeater equipment; this does not add a new Repeater object or Army carrier relationship.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Modifier (**MOD**) is a bonus (+) or penalty (-)
factsEvidence: A named ReRoll is one die from the relevant Roll, not a Command Token reroll
reviews.caveat: Modifier and ReRoll terminology distinguishes a named reroll from Command Token expenditure; it describes no physical Token or deployed object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Coordinated Order lets up to four eligible Troopers act together
factsEvidence: Name one participating Trooper as Spearhead and place a Spearhead Token beside them.
reviews.caveat: A Spearhead Token marks the role of an existing participant. The Targetless/Deployable exception allows different target points, not inferred object identities or sources.

reviews.summaryEvidence: After the Initiative Roll, the players deploy their Troopers before the game begins
factsEvidence: Rules such as [[skill:forward-deployment|Forward Deployment]]
reviews.caveat: Deployment Phase governs reserve ordering and adjustments such as Command Tokens. It does not define new deployed objects or deliveries.
